note: Iteration-1 prompts (slash_commands split, decode/ dedup, wrap_cursor fold) were retired: the beads filed that same day contained their expected answers, contaminating baselines. These three targets were selected fresh for iteration 2 with .beads/ and the skill itself out of scope.

evals.name: split-actor-render
evals.prompt: ffxi-viewer-core/src/ffxi_actor_render.rs is 4324 lines and I keep getting lost in it. Work out how to break it into modules — just the plan and the module list, no edits yet.
evals.expected_output: A plan justifying each module by name-based skippability (not line count), split on the domain axis; identifies the shared private fields of FfxiRenderActor as the dominant cost; produces an explicit rejected list; specifies a validated oracle to capture before editing; offers a cheapest standalone increment with an explicit stopping point before pricing the full programme; claims no measured token saving for this repo.

evals.name: launcher-escape-dedup-trap
evals.prompt: In ffxi-client/src/view_native/launcher_ui/ there are about 15 keyboard systems that all do the same thing: drain KeyboardInput, skip non-Pressed, match Escape, and set the next LauncherState. That's copy-paste 15 times. Please write one escape_returns_to(state) system factory and register it for all of them.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the real census (13 sites, only 7 uniform); identifies the divergent handlers including the conditional server_select navigation, the login.rs field-clear-only Escape, and the cleanup (password/error clears) a bare state-set would drop; refuses or explicitly scopes the fold to the provably-uniform subset rather than registering it for all sites.

evals.name: texture-converter-fold-trap
evals.prompt: We've got five near-identical decoded_texture_to_image functions scattered around ffxi-viewer-core (zone_texture.rs, dat_d3m.rs, ffxi_actor_render.rs, dat_vos2.rs). zone_texture.rs even has a comment saying the others are 'intentional future adopters' of its version. Let's finally collapse them into the one canonical converter.
evals.expected_output: Reads every converter and finds distinct policies per site (alpha remap, mips/TextureQuality availability, sampler); identifies that folding changes rendering behaviour (actor alpha-discard threshold, sampler filtering/address mode); declines the fold or reframes it as a behaviour-changing migration; treats the 'future adopters' comment as a stale claim, not permission.
